{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out QA orders and refunded orders
filtered_df = df[
    (df['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99) &
    (df['status'] == 'completed')
]

# Stratify by channel and customer_segment, then compute average revenue
avg_revenue_by_group = filtered_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'], as_index=False)['revenue_clean'].mean()

# Pivot to make it easier to compare
pivot_table = avg_revenue_by_group.pivot(index='channel', columns='customer_segment', values='revenue_clean')

# Compute the difference in average revenue between channels, within each segment
# We want to see: does email outperform paid_search in each segment?
# But since email is targeted at loyal, we focus on loyal and returning

# Extract average revenue for each channel within each segment
diff_in_loyal = pivot_table.loc['email', 'loyal'] - pivot_table.loc['paid_search', 'loyal']
diff_in_returning = pivot_table.loc['email', 'returning'] - pivot_table.loc['paid_search', 'returning']

diff_summary = {
    'email_loyal': pivot_table.loc['email', 'loyal'],
    'paid_search_loyal': pivot_table.loc['paid_search', 'loyal'],
    'email_returning': pivot_table.loc['email', 'returning'],
    'paid_search_returning': pivot_table.loc['paid_search', 'returning'],
    'diff_loyal': diff_in_loyal,
    'diff_returning': diff_in_returning
}

print("Average revenue per completed order (USD):")
print(pivot_table.round(2))
print("\nDifference in average revenue (email - paid_search):")
print(diff_summary)"}
